notes: Identity independently checked: title Re-analysis of Genetic Risks for Chronic Fatigue Syndrome From 23andMe Data Finds Few Remain; Felice L. Bedford and Bastian Greshake Tzovaras; DOI 10.3389/fped.2021.590040; published 18 March 2021. Document labelled OPINION, but contains the authors’ primary reanalysis (Method, Results, Table 1, Discussion), not merely an abstract or secondary quotation. Supplied canonical text spans all four article pages and references. No PDF supplied. Target mapped by named gene and unique rsID, independently of row order or numeric matching. Input locator p. 5 differs from article pagination: Table 1 is p. 3 of this four-page article. Primary comparison is comparable 23andMe control; printed frequency ratio 1.98 retained without conversion to requested OR. ALFA is an additional control with printed alternative ratio 1.81, not merged into the primary comparison. No inferential test or p value is reported for this comparison: paper uses descriptive ratio-of-two criterion. Reported success is authors’ explicit gene-specific retention verdict, not an inference of statistical significance. Original side and replication N are unassigned placeholders and must not overwrite verified fields. Table 1 prints 1.98 for MORN2 with the 23andMe control, whereas authors include MORN2 among the three meeting at-least-double criteria and describe ratios as about 2.0. Printed value and narrative verdict are both preserved; no rounding correction applied.
